clue.text: Way in front when approaching a town

definitions.meaning: far in the lead, an idiom for being well ahead of rivals
read literally: as you near a town, its roads lie before you

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a literal take on the idiom: driving towards a town, the roads are in front of you.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an idiom for being far better than rivals, and a literal picture of roads lying before a traveller nearing a town.

clue.text: Instrument needed to make sound wine cask

indicators.note: the clue asks us to voice the phrase, so what we hear is spelt differently from what is written

parts.note: SACK is an old word for a dry sherry-type wine, and a BUTT is a large cask

explanation.surface: A musician says you need an instrument to make the noise of a wine barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: SACK (old white wine) plus BUTT (a big barrel) said aloud gives the instrument's name, which has only one T. 'needed' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The early trombone of Renaissance music is a brass instrument with a slide.

clue.text: Pakistanis use it to buy curried purée

indicators.note: food that is curried has been spiced and stirred up, so the letters of the next word are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone in Pakistan pays for a portion of spicy mashed food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curried' rearranges the letters of 'purée' (accent dropped).
explanation.definitionFit: The currency unit of Pakistan, as of India, is what shoppers there pay with.

clue.text: In sympathy with the French

parts.note: read as 'the French way of saying in sympathy with': a borrowed French phrase meaning in harmony with someone

explanation.definitionFit: A French-derived phrase used in English meaning in close accord or harmony, so in sympathy with another person.

clue.text: Give autograph as a gesture

definitions.meaning: to write one's name on something
a movement or signal conveying meaning, such as a nod

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to write one's name on a document, and a motion or signal made to communicate.

clue.text: If immersion heater fails to provide it, there's trouble

definitions.text: If immersion heater fails to provide it
definitions.meaning: an immersion heater is a household tank heater; if it breaks there is nothing warm from the taps
being in difficulty, as in the idiom 'in deep water'

explanation.walkthrough: An immersion heater is the electric element in a British household hot tank; when it fails, the warm supply stops, which is also a predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: what a tank heater supplies for baths, and an idiom for being in a scrape or in disgrace.

clue.text: Warning signal for a physician to HM

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification
Her Majesty the Queen is ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: An alarm goes off as a doctor attends the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' and 'to' are links. ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the crossword's standard Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: On traffic lights the middle colour cautions drivers that red is coming.

clue.text: Put down as reserve

definitions.meaning: to set something to one side, laying it out of the way
to keep back for later use

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to set an object down out of the way, and to save something for future use.

clue.text: Engineer demands non-ersatz food

parts.note: CE is short for civil engineer
something not ersatz is not a substitute, so genuine

explanation.surface: An engineer insists on proper, unprocessed meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demands' is a link. Ersatz means fake or substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakfast grain foods such as cornflakes or oats are a kind of food.

clue.text: Make correct reproduction for author's safeguard

parts.note: a reproduction is a duplicate made of an original
to put right, rectify

explanation.surface: Fix a facsimile so a writer's work is protected.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives 'Make correct' first, but the answer puts the reproduction first; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal protection over published work is a writer's guard against unauthorised reprinting.

clue.text: Fire idle big-head for starters

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is taken, as a starter opens a meal

parts.note: to idle is to laze around

explanation.surface: Sack the lazy, arrogant one to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' looks like a verb (dismiss) but is the noun, a conflagration.
explanation.definitionFit: A large fierce outbreak of flames is a conflagration.

clue.text: Sounds like someone's text-messaged

definitions.meaning: what a mobile does when someone is sent a text, alerting them

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: short electronic tones, and what a mobile phone emits when someone receives a text.

clue.text: In such a match there's no easy target

definitions.text: In such a match there's no easy target

parts.words: In such a match there's no easy target
parts.note: read one way, a contest played honestly, with no soft target; read the other, a phrase for a legitimate target of attack or ridicule

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a person or thing regarded as a legitimate target, and also suggests a sporting match played honestly.

clue.text: Display tawdry items as well

parts.note: tat is cheap, tasteless goods
too means also

explanation.walkthrough: 'Display' looks like a verb but is the noun: a military show, like the Edinburgh one.
explanation.definitionFit: An evening military pageant with bands and marching is a public spectacle.

clue.text: Vary test layout? That's a mockery!

indicators.note: a new layout arranges the letters of the two preceding words afresh

explanation.surface: Someone protests that changing the format of an exam is a farce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layout' signals rearranging VARYTEST; 'That's a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotesque parody or distorted imitation is a mockery.

clue.text: To write one's own bequests requires obstinacy

definitions.meaning: read literally: a testament drawn up by oneself, without a lawyer

explanation.walkthrough: 'requires' is a link; the first reading splits the answer into 'self' and 'will' (testament).
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a testament drawn up personally, and stubborn determination to have one's own way.

clue.text: Flat out

parts.note: read one way, an apartment emptied completely; read the other, going as fast as possible

explanation.definitionFit: Driving flat out means at maximum velocity, with the accelerator pressed to the floor.

clue.text: Herb makes Jack put Scott Joplin piece on

parts.note: a jack tar is a sailor, so TAR
Scott Joplin wrote piano rags such as The Entertainer

explanation.surface: A plant inspires a sailor to play a ragtime tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' and 'put' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An aromatic plant with an aniseed flavour, used in French cooking, is a culinary herb.

clue.text: Make many drink gin? Rubbish!

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
to lap is to drink with the tongue, as a cat does
a gin is a snare or trap for game

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at forcing a crowd to swallow spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' is a link. 'gin' is not the spirit but a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretentious empty talk is nonsense.

clue.text: A bit rough to axe penny? Say why!

parts.note: to axe is to chop

indicators.note: speak the next word: we hear a letter's name

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like Y

explanation.surface: A cost-cutter asks why cutting a single coin is harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; 'Say' turns 'why' into the letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that is choppy has small rough waves, so it is somewhat turbulent.

clue.text: Right to enter as asylum-seekers?

indicators.note: the word for a right goes inside the word 'as'

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A question about whether refugees have the entitlement to come in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks like an entitlement to asylum but is the legal term for a claim on property. The question mark flags a definition by example: refugees are foreigners.
explanation.definitionFit: People seeking refuge are foreigners from another country, an example of the class.

clue.text: Some students go up there to tan, maybe

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up reads the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: part means some of
NUS is the National Union of Students

explanation.surface: A few students climb to a spot for sunbathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go up' reads PARTNUS backwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheltered sunny spot is a place where one goes for sunbathing.

clue.text: Commence shooting when it's warmer

definitions.meaning: something that heats a room, such as a grate with flames

explanation.walkthrough: 'when it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to begin firing weapons, and an unenclosed hearth that heats a room.

clue.text: Petty cash needed for milk deliveries

definitions.meaning: a small sum kept to give change
a milk ... is the small electric van British milkmen used for doorstep deliveries

explanation.walkthrough: 'needed' is a link. A milk float is the quiet electric van British milkmen drove on doorstep rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a small sum of cash kept in a till for change, and the electric van used by a milkman.

clue.text: Flower name found at the back

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A plant label is discovered at the rear of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' is a link; 'Flower' is the plant, not a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautical term for behind a ship, towards the rear.

clue.text: Supplement to appear in next "radio times"

indicators.note: the answer is found within the words that follow, appearing among their letters

explanation.surface: An advert insert will run in the next issue of the listings magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to appear in' points inside 'next radio'. Radio Times is a British TV and radio listings magazine; an extra also appears in shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Something additional is a supplement, like an extra charge or edition.

clue.text: A fruit served up with fish

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up reads the letters upwards

parts.note: a nut is a dry fruit

explanation.surface: A waiter brings fruit alongside a seafood dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses ANUT; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A large ocean food fish often sold in cans.

clue.text: Irishman and I love to hold court

parts.note: Pat, short for Patrick, is a stock Irish name
O is love, zero in tennis scores

explanation.surface: An Irishman and the speaker enjoy holding forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold' is a link; 'hold court' suggests presiding, but court is a courtyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A paved outdoor area next to a house is a courtyard.

clue.text: As a petty tyrant, I regulate production

indicators.note: production here means making something new from the letters given

explanation.surface: A small-time despot boasts of controlling output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' rearranges IREGULATE; 'As a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nazi district governor; by extension an overbearing official.

clue.text: Highlight for model Californian politician?

parts.note: a standard is a model to follow
LA is Los Angeles in California
MP is a member of parliament

explanation.surface: A question on whether a Californian lawmaker is a model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link. 'Highlight' is a light that stands high, not the best part.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall floor lamp gives light from a high position.
